question.problem:
Find the $21$st term of the following arithmetic sequence.

$$
-3,\,-7,\,-11,\,-15,\,…
$$
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

First, we will write the formula for the $n$th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

$$
-3,\,-7,\,-11,\,-15,\,…,
$$

we see that the first term is ${a}_{1}=-3$ and the common difference is 

$$
d=-7-(-3)=-4.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-3+(n-1)(-4) \\  & =-3-4n+4 \\  & =1-4n\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use our formula to find the $21$st term. All we have to do is substitute $n=21:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =1-4n \\ {a}_{21} & =1-4(21) \\  & =1-84 \\  & =-83\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $21$st term of the sequence is ${a}_{21}=-83.$
